name: quenching
description: OKF-centric knowledge-base aligner for the Claude Code surface of any repository. It acts on three fronts — the docs/ OKF bundle, the native specs/ spec-driven workspace, and the .claude/ command surface — and every front has exactly one align: /quenching:knowledge:align, /quenching:specs:align, /quenching:components:align, with the root /align conducting all three in dependency order on a single confirmation and looping across them until nothing changes anywhere. Each align is probe-first, so a conformant front costs a couple of tool calls and stops. Around them: inserts knowledge into the right home, curates a fixed A–Z glossary, drains project memory into docs, refactors CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md into thin pointers, imports external sources as OKF docs, generates and validates a complete documentation site through the plan/write/review/build family, mints and measures commands, subagents and hooks, and drives the spec cycle (create → develop → execute → conclude, with cycle conducting stages in one run, plus triage and status) with the bundle as its knowledge substrate — entirely native, no external CLI, no delta, no separate spec store: a spec writes its durable rules straight into docs/standards/, isolated on a real git branch whose per-task commits it records, and one deterministic stdlib Python entry point, one pillar per front, gives the commands their rails behind a uniform --json and strict exit codes. Thirty-eight commands, one file per entry point — the path is the identity, no skills/ tree and no wrapper — each keeping default invocation under /quenching:knowledge:*, /quenching:specs:*, /quenching:components:*, /quenching:git:* and the root /align. Every repository that adopts it looks the same.
